citation: Gorard, S., Siddiqui, N., & See, B. H. (2015). Philosophy for Children: Evaluation report and Executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluators: Durham University.)
report_number: EEF project: Philosophy for Children (P4C / SAPERE), July 2015
design: School-level cluster RCT (waitlist control); 48 primary schools (22 intervention, 26 control) across England; Years 4-5 cohorts (KS2, grades 3-6); subjects = KS2 reading, writing/GPS, maths and CAT4 cognitive ability. Primary attainment outcome = original Year 5 pupils' KS2 results (n=1529) adjusted for prior KS1.
problems: EEF effect sizes are standardised mean differences of KS1->KS2 gain z-scores (pretest-adjusted), labelled 'Hedges g' in the report (p.17), but they are computed at the PUPIL level and do NOT come from a multilevel model, so they are NOT cluster-adjusted. n_clusters recorded (22 treatment + 26 control schools = 48). ICC left null: the only ICC in the report (0.2) is a power-calculation assumption, not a reported design-effect ICC (spec: never guess an ICC). g_var/g_se below are the naive (non-cluster) variances for central Hedges-2007 correction. FSM-subgroup rows (Tables 8-10) are a pre-specified non-randomised subgroup (the FSM cases were not randomised as such, per p.20) and are reported as additional contrasts. CAT4 (Table 11) is a cognitive-ability/reasoning test rather than a subject-attainment test; included and labelled accordingly. The report does not give raw subject means/SDs for KS2 (only standardised gain z-scores), so mean/sd fields use the gain z-score values; the standardising SD is the pooled (Total-row) gain SD.

effect_sizes.arm_label: P4C (SAPERE) vs waitlist control - whole cohort
effect_sizes.test_name: Key Stage 2 reading (National Pupil Database), KS1->KS2 standardised gain
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's 'Effect' size = Hedges g (p.17) = (gain z T - gain z C)/pooled gain SD = (0.06-(-0.05))/0.90 = 0.12; standardised by Total-row gain z-score SD (0.90). J=0.9995 (df=1527). g_var = naive Var(g)=J^2*((n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c)+d^2/(2(n_t+n_c))).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.20, Table 5; exec summary Table p.4
effect_sizes.notes: Headline result: ~+2 months progress in reading. Reported by report as Hedges g.

effect_sizes.arm_label: P4C (SAPERE) vs waitlist control - whole cohort
effect_sizes.test_name: Key Stage 2 maths (National Pupil Database), KS1->KS2 standardised gain
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's 'Effect' size = Hedges g = (0.04-(-0.04))/0.78 = 0.10; standardised by Total-row gain z-score SD (0.78). J=0.9995. g_var = naive Var(g).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.20, Table 7; exec summary Table p.4
effect_sizes.notes: Headline result: ~+2 months progress in maths. Reported by report as Hedges g. maths -> STEM.

effect_sizes.g_method: Report's 'Effect' size = Hedges g = (0.01-(-0.02))/0.84 = 0.03; standardised by Total-row gain z-score SD (0.84). J=0.9995. g_var = naive Var(g).

effect_sizes.test_name: CAT4 (Cognitive Abilities Test, 4th ed., GL Assessment), overall pre->post gain
effect_sizes.g_method: Report's 'Effect' size = Hedges g = (gain T - gain C)/pooled SD = (2.22-1.70)/7.46 = 0.07; standardised by Total-row gain SD (7.46). mean_t/mean_c = gain scores; sd from gain SDs. J=0.9997. g_var = naive Var(g).
effect_sizes.notes: CAT4 is a cognitive-ability/reasoning test, not a subject-achievement test (secondary outcome). Effect driven by initial Year 5 cohort (Year5 g=+0.14 Table 17; Year4 g=-0.01 Table 16) and by the verbal subscale (g=+0.08 Table 12). Subscales: verbal +0.08, quantitative -0.01, non-verbal +0.04, spatial +0.07 (Tables 12-15). outcome_subject set to Other since it is not a subject-content achievement test; central filtering can reclassify/drop.
